Rashi on Eruvin 52a:10:1.english: That was also taught - That we are dealing with a case where he has two houses, and between them are two Shabbat limits.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:10:2.hebrew: כיון שהחזיק בדרך קנה עירוב - אף אם לא אמר ״שביתתי בסוף התחום״, וחזר:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:10:2.english: Once he set out on the way, he acquired an eiruv - Even if he did not say, “My Shabbat residence is at the end of the [Shabbat] limit,” and he returned [home].

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:11:1.hebrew: יתר על כן - אפילו לא החזיק בדרך, אלא אמר לצאת, והחזירו חברו ואמר: ״לין פה״:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:11:1.english: Furthermore - Even if he did not set out on the way, but [only] intended to leave, and his fellow turned him back and said: “Lodge here”:

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:12:1.hebrew: לומר כ"ע לא פליגי דצריך - שיאמר לו חברו "לין פה", כדקתני מתניתין בדר' יהודה: "והחזירו חברו" — דהשתא, ודאי משום צינה וחמה הוא דהדר ביה, ודעתיה למקני שביתה בסוף התחום, ואע"פ שלא אמר. אבל אם חזר מעצמו, איכא למימר נמלך, ולא קנה שביתה לשם, דאפילו גלוי דעתא ליכא, והרי הוא כבני עירו:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:12:1.english: With regard to saying, everyone agrees that it is necessary - That his friend say to him, "Lodge here," as the Mishnah teaches according to Rabbi Yehuda: "and his friend turned him back." For now, it is certainly on account of cold or heat that he turned back, and his intention was to acquire Shabbat residence at the end of the Shabbat limit, even though he did not say [so explicitly]. But if he returned on his own, it can be said that he changed his mind and did not acquire Shabbat residence there, for there is not even a disclosure of intent, and he is like the [other] residents of his town.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:12:2.hebrew: כי פליגי להחזיק - והיינו "יתר על כן": אפילו לא החזיק בדרך, אלא שאמר לו חברו "לין פה" — ששמע ממנו שהיה רוצה לצאת, ואמר לו: "לין פה בביתך הלילה משום צינה":
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:12:2.english: When they disagree [is with regard to] setting out - And this is [the meaning of] "Furthermore": Even if he did not set out on the way, but rather his fellow said to him, "Spend the night here" — as he heard from him that he wished to set out, and said to him, "Spend the night here in your house tonight on account of the cold."

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:13:1.hebrew: ורב יוסף אמר להחזיק כ"ע לא פליגי דצריך כי פליגי לומר - "לין פה" — דלר' יהודה, אם החזיק בדרך, אע"פ שלא אמר לו חברו "לין פה" אלא שחזר מעצמו, כמאן דאמר "שביתתי במקום פלוני" דמי. והחזירו חברו דקתני מתניתין לר"י לאו דוקא, דה"ה לחזר מעצמו, אלא אורחא דמילתא נקט. אבל ר' יוסי בר' יהודה תרוייהו בעי: חזקה ואמירה, (והכי קאמר: מצאו חברו שהתחיל לצאת, ואמר לו חברו: "לין פה עמדי הלילה"; וקסבר רב יוסף: ר' יוסי בר' יהודה להחמיר, ולא תנן בברייתא "יתר על כן" "ואפילו", אלא הכי תנן: ר' יוסי אומר מצאו חברו כו'). כך שמעתי. והרבה גמגומין יש, דקשיא ליה: לר' יוסי מאי "יתר על כן" ומאי "אפילו"? ויש מתרצין דרבי יוסי לא בעי חזקה כולי האי כדר' יהודה. אבל אמרי נואש הן, דפסיעה אחת חוץ לביתו הויא חזקה, ובציר מהכי ליכא חזקה. ועוד, רב יוסף אמר דבחזקה לא פליגי אלא בלומר, וא"כ אף בחזקה פליגי: ל"א, ולא שמעתיו: אמר רבה, לומר "שביתתי בתוך התחום" כ"ע לא פליגי דצריך זה החוזר לומר כן; וכי פליג ר' יוסי ואתא לאקולי, אחזקה פליג, דשמעיה לר' יהודה דאמר "החזיק", ואתא איהו למימר אפילו מצאו חברו שהיה רוצה להחזיק ולא הניחו קנה עירוב, ובלבד שיאמר "שביתתי לשם", דהואיל והיה רוצה לצאת, חשבינן ליה כיוצא, והוי עני. ורב יוסף אמר: להחזיק לא פליגי, דודאי חזקה בעינן, דאי לא החזיק לא הוי עני; כי פליגי — לומר, דר' יהודה בעי שיאמר "שביתתי לשם", וארישא דמתניתין קאי דפריש בה "ואמר שביתתי בעיקרו", ולא איצטריך למיהדר ומיתנייא בסיפא, ואתא ר' יוסי למימר: אפילו לא אמר מידי קני, הואיל והחזיק, דגלוי דעתא קנייה היא. וא"ת: כיון דלרבי יהודה באומר "שביתתי במקום פלוני" קאמר, אמאי פליג ר"מ עליה ומשוי ליה חמר גמל? ר"מ לית ליה חזקה כי האי גוונא, אלא בא בדרך ממש, אבל האי כעשיר משוי ליה. וקסבר ר"מ: כל שהוא עשיר, והיה לו לערב בפת, ולא עירב בפת אלא באמירה, הפסיד באמירתו אלפים שהיה לו לעבר הלז מביתו, שסילק עצמו מרוח זו, ובמקום שביתתו לא נשתכר דלאו עירוב הוא, ואין לו אלא אלפים הללו. ונראין הדברים דר' מאיר אכל מי שהוא עשיר פליג, ובאומר "שביתתי במקום פלוני", מדקתני: "כל שיש בידו לערב כו'". דאי ס"ד ר"מ עני משוי ליה להאי, וטעמא משום דמספקא לן היכא ניחא ליה הוא, הואיל ולא אמר — אם כן מאי "כל"? הא לא משכחת לה הך ספיקא אלא בהך לחודיה שיצא וחזר, "והרי זה חמר גמל" מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:13:1.english: And Rav Yosef said: With regard to setting out, everyone agrees that it is necessary; when they disagree is with regard to saying - [With regard to his friend saying,] "Spend the night here" — for according to Rabbi Yehuda, if he set out on the way, even though his friend did not say to him, "Spend the night here," but rather he returned on his own, he is considered like one who says, "My Shabbat residence is in such-and-such place." And that which the Mishnah teaches according to Rabbi Yehuda, "and another caused him to return," is not exact, for the same applies to one who returned on his own; rather, [the Mishnah] merely stated common practice. But Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, requires both: setting out and saying [by his friend] (and this is what [the Baraita] means: 'His friend found him having begun to set out, and his friend said to him: Spend the night here with me tonight'; and Rav Yosef maintains that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, came to be stringent, and we do not learn in the Baraita 'Furthermore' and 'even,' but rather this is how it is taught: 'Rabbi Yosei says: His friend found him, etc.'). Thus I heard. But there are many difficulties [with this explanation], for it is difficult: according to Rabbi Yosei, what is [the meaning of] 'Furthermore' and what is [the meaning of] 'even'? And some attempt to resolve it [by saying] that Rabbi Yosei does not require as much of a setting out as Rabbi Yehuda [requires]. But these are words of despair [untenable answers], for taking a single step outside his house constitutes setting out, and less than this cannot be considered setting out. Furthermore, Rav Yosef said that with regard to setting out they do not disagree, but only with regard to saying; and if so, [under this proposed resolution] they would disagree about setting out as well: Another explanation, and I did not hear it [from my teachers]: Rabba said: with regard to saying, "My Shabbat residence is within the limit," everyone agrees that this person who returns is required to say so; and when Rabbi Yosei disagrees and comes to be lenient, he disagrees about setting out — for he heard Rabbi Yehuda say that he must have set out, and he came to say that even if his friend found him when he wanted to set out and did not allow him, he acquires an eiruv, provided that he says, "My Shabbat residence is there," because since he wanted to set out, we consider him like one who set out, and he has [the status of] a pauper. And Rav Yosef said: with regard to setting out, they do not disagree, for we certainly require setting out, because if he did not set out, he would not be a pauper; where they disagree is with regard to saying: Rabbi Yehuda requires that he say, "My Shabbat residence is there" — and [Rabbi Yehuda's statement] is based on the first clause of the Mishnah, where it was explicitly stated: "and he said: My Shabbat residence is at its base," and it was not necessary to repeat it and teach it in the latter clause — and Rabbi Yosei came to say: even if he did not say anything at all, he acquires [the eiruv], since he set out, because a demonstration of intent is an effective acquisition. And if you say: since according to Rabbi Yehuda he is speaking of [a case where] he says, "My Shabbat residence is in such-and-such place," why does Rabbi Meir disagree with him and render him [restricted as both] a donkey driver and a camel driver? Rabbi Meir does not accept setting out of this kind [as granting pauper status], but only one who was actually traveling on the road; but this person, [Rabbi Meir] treats him as a wealthy person. And Rabbi Meir maintains: anyone who is wealthy and should have established an eiruv with bread, and did not establish an eiruv with bread but rather through speech, has lost through his statement the two thousand [cubits] that he had on the other side of his house, because he removed himself from that direction; yet in the place of his Shabbat residence he gained nothing, because [speech] is not a valid eiruv [for a wealthy person], and he has only these two thousand [cubits between his house and the designated place]. And it appears that Rabbi Meir disagrees with regard to anyone who is a wealthy person, and where he said, "My Shabbat residence is in such-and-such place," since [the Mishnah] taught: "Anyone who has the means to establish an eiruv, etc." For if it should enter your mind that Rabbi Meir treats this person as a pauper, and the reason is because it is uncertain to us where it is preferable to him since he did not say [where his residence should be] — if so, what is [the meaning of] "Anyone"? Behold, you cannot find this uncertainty except in this [case] alone, where he went out and returned; [rather than "Anyone who has the means to establish an eiruv... is a donkey driver and camel driver", the Mishnah] should have stated: "and he is a donkey driver and camel driver"!

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:14:1.english: Returned - [This] implies that he did not acquire a Shabbat residence at all.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:14:2.english: Established - This implies that he acquired [his Shabbat residence]:

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:16:1.hebrew: כמאן - ללישנא קמא דפרשי, דרב יוסף אליבא דר' יוסי תרתי בעי — אמירה דלין פה וחזקה — הכי בעי ליה: כמאן אזלה הא דעולא, דבעי תרתי: שהחזיק — היינו חזקה, והחזירו חברו — היינו לי פה:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:16:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion] - According to the first version that they explained, that Rav Yosef [held that] according to Rabbi Yosei, two [conditions] are required — the statement of "Lodge here" and setting out [on the way] — this is what [the Gemara] is asking: In accordance with whom does this [ruling] of Ulla go, which requires two [conditions]: "that he set out" — that is setting out [on the way], and "his fellow returned him" — that is [his fellow saying,] "Lodge here"?

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:16:2.hebrew: כרב יוסף אליבא דר' יוסי בר' יהודה - דבעי תרתי, והוא הדין לרבה אליבא דר' יהודה, אלא חדא מינייהו נקט. וללישנא בתרא, הכי פירושא: כמאן אזלא הא דעולא, דלא בעי למימר "שביתתי במקום פלוני", דקאמר "אע"פ שמוחזר", דמשמע לגמרי? כרב יוסף ואליבא דרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, דאמר: לא בעינן לומר. (הג"ה: ואהך לישנא ליכא למימר "כרבה ואליבא דר' יהודה", דבין רבה ובין רב יוסף תרוייהו סבירא להו דרבי יהודה תרתי בעי. עד כאן):
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:16:2.english: According to Rav Yosef, and in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda - For he requires two [conditions]. And the same would apply to Rabba according to Rabbi Yehuda, but [the Gemara] cited [only] one of them. And according to the second version, this is the explanation: In accordance with whom does this [ruling] of Ulla go, which does not require [a person] to say, "My Shabbat residence is in such-and-such place" — for he said, "Although he was returned," which implies completely? In accordance with Rav Yosef, and according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, who said: We do not require [him] to say [a declaration]. (Gloss: And according to this version, one cannot say [that it could also be] in accordance with Rabba according to Rabbi Yehuda, for both Rabba and Rav Yosef hold that Rabbi Yehuda requires two [conditions]. End of gloss.)

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:17:1.english: Ishtata - [This is] the name of a person.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:17:2.hebrew: כי הוה אזיל - לביתיה, ובתוך ד' אלפים הוה:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:17:2.english: When he was going - To his home, and [it] was within four thousand [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:17:3.hebrew: נחת דרגא - מעלה מן הכבש, שהיה יורד מן העליה, דהוה ליה החזיק בדרך:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:17:3.english: He descended a step - A step of the staircase, as he was descending from the upper story, so that he would be [considered as having] set out on the way.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:17:4.english: Lodge here - Spend the night here.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:1:1.hebrew: מאי דעתיך - דעשיר את, ואמרת שביתתי במקום פלוני:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:1:1.english: What is your opinion - That you are a wealthy person, and you said: "My residence is in such-and-such a place"?

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:2:1.hebrew: והא אמר רב נחמן - דלא שרי ר' יהודה אלא במקומי, ותניא כוותיה דרב נחמן לעיל:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:2:1.english: But didn’t Rav Naḥman say - That Rabbi Yehuda permitted [it] only “in my place,” and it was taught [in a baraita] in accordance with Rav Naḥman above.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:3:1.hebrew: שבת - שקונה שביתה ברגליו, יש לו ד' אמות לקניית בית, לבד מאלפים לכל רוח:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:3:1.english: [One who] established residence - One who acquires residence with his feet has four cubits for the acquisition of a dwelling, aside from two thousand [cubits] in each direction.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:4:1.english: It is a stringency - For he loses four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:6:1.hebrew: מי שיצא - מעירו לילך בעיר אחרת שמערבין בה, שסמוכה לעירו בתוך ד' אלפים:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:6:1.english: One who set out - From his town to go to another town for which an eiruv is established, which is adjacent to his town within four thousand [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 52a:6:2.hebrew: הוא מותר לילך - ואע"פ שלא אמר כלום, כדפירשתי לעיל. דכיון שיש לו לשם בית, ודאי לא עקר דעתו מהליכתו, ונתכוון לקנות שביתה בסוף התחום, והוי כעני האומר "שביתתי במקום פלוני" וקנה, דהא עני הוא, דהחזיק בדרך. ולרבי מאיר, ודאי עני הוא, ואי אמר הוי קני; אבל השתא, דיכול היה לערב ולומר "שביתתי במקום פלוני" ולא אמר, מספקא לן אי הוה דעתו לקנות שביתה בסוף התחום או בביתו, והרי זה חמר גמל, שאין לו אלא אלפים שבין ביתו לסוף התחום; אבל אלפים שמעבר ביתו לצד השני הפסיד, דשמא בסוף התחום קנה, ומסוף התחום נמי לא קנה אלפים לצד עיר האחרת, שמא לא קנה שביתה כאן כי אם בביתו:
Rashi on Eruvin 52a:6:2.english: He is permitted to go - And even though he said nothing, as I explained above; for since he has a house there, he certainly did not abandon his intention to make his trip, and he intended to acquire [Shabbat] residence at the end of the [Shabbat] limit, and he is like a poor person who says, "My Shabbat residence is in such-and-such place," and acquires [it], as he is a poor person, since he embarked on the way. And according to Rabbi Meir, he is certainly a poor person, and had he spoken, he would have acquired [it]; but now, that he was able to establish an eiruv and say, "My Shabbat residence is in such-and-such place," and did not say [it], it is uncertain to us whether his intention was to acquire [Shabbat] residence at the end of the limit or in his house. And behold, this person is [in the status of] a donkey driver–camel driver, who has only the two thousand [cubits] between his house and the end of the limit; but the two thousand [cubits] beyond his house to the other side he forfeits, lest he acquired [residence] at the end of the limit; and from the end of the limit as well, he did not acquire two thousand [cubits] toward the other town, lest he did not acquire Shabbat residence here, but rather in his house.

Tosafot on Eruvin 52a:13:1.hebrew: לומר כ"ע לא פליגי דצריך - פי' ר"ת: לומר "עת חמה הוא ועת צינה הוא", דכיון שהחזירו מטעם זה — אם כן, כיון דעתו לילך כשתעבור חמה וצינה, ולא יצא מתורת עני. אבל אם בלא טעם החזירו — אם כן, לגמרי נתייאש מלילך, ויצא מתורת עני, אע"פ שהחזיק בדרך. ורב יוסף אמר: "להחזיק כולי עלמא לא פליגי דצריך, כי פליגי — לומר" — דסבר רב יוסף: כיון שמחמת חמה וצינה הוא חוזר, אם כן נתייאש לגמרי מלילך, ולא קנה העירוב לרבי יהודה, אלא כשחוזר בלא טעם. "יתר על כן אמר ר' יוסי" — דאפילו הכי קנה עירוב. והוה ליה לרב יוסף למנקט: "כי פליגי — באומר", אלא נקט במילתיה דרב יוסף "לומר" אגב מילתיה דרבה. ודייק רב יוסף מדלא הזכיר ר' יהודה עת צינה ועת חמה, ורבי יוסי הזכיר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 52a:13:1.english: "With regard to saying, everyone agrees that it is necessary" - Rabbeinu Tam explains: [This means for his friend] to say [to him], "It is a time of heat, it is a time of cold," for since [his friend] turned him back for this reason, if so, he still intended to go when the heat and cold pass, and he did not depart from the legal status of a poor person. But if [his friend] turned him back without a reason, if so, he completely gave up on going and departed from the legal status of a poor person, even though he had set out on the way. And [as for the statement:] "And Rav Yosef said: With regard to setting out, everyone agrees that it is necessary; where they disagree is with regard to saying" — for Rav Yosef maintains: Since he is returning due to heat and cold, if so, he completely gave up on going, and he did not acquire the eiruv according to Rabbi Yehuda unless he returns without a reason. [And when the baraita states:] "Furthermore, Rabbi Yosei said" — [it means] that even so, he acquired the eiruv. And Rav Yosef should have formulated [his statement as]: "Where they disagree is regarding one who says [this]"; rather, "to say" was formulated in Rav Yosef's statement on account of Rabba's statement. And Rav Yosef deduced [this] from the fact that Rabbi Yehuda did not mention "a time of cold and a time of heat," whereas Rabbi Yosei did mention [it].

Tosafot on Eruvin 52a:14:1.hebrew: כמאן אזלא הא דאמר עולא אף על פי שמוחזר מוחזק כמאן כרב יוסף ואליבא דרבי יוסי - מלשון אע"פ דייק, דחזר מחמת חמה וצינה, ולא קנה עירוב לרבי יהודה. וכרבה לא אתיא, דלכ"ע בעי רבה שיאמר: "עת צינה הוא", ואי דאמר "עת צינה", לא שייך לשון "אע"פ". ופי' זה דחוק, ופי' אחרון דרש"י נראה לר"י עיקר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 52a:14:1.english: "In accordance with whose [opinion] does that which Ulla said go: 'Although he is returned, he is [considered] set out'? In accordance with whose [opinion]? In accordance with Rav Yosef, and according to Rabbi Yosei" - From the wording "although," [the Gemara] deduces that he returned due to heat and cold, and did not acquire an eruv according to Rabbi Yehuda. And it cannot follow Rabba, for according to everyone Rabba requires that [the friend] say: "It is a time of cold"; and if he said "It is a time of cold," the phrasing "although" is not applicable. And this explanation is forced, and the last explanation of Rashi appears to the Ri to be primary.

Tosafot on Eruvin 52a:4:1.hebrew: האי להקל להחמיר הוא - ואם תאמר: תיקשי ליה לשמואל דסוף כיצד מעברין (לקמן עירובין דף סא:), דאמר: שבת בעיר חריבה, לרבנן מהלך את כולה וחוצה לה אלפים אמה; הניח עירובו בעיר חריבה, אין לו ממקומו אלא אלפים אמה? וי"ל: מכל מקום, בסתמא כי אורחיה, כשאין נותן עירובו בעיר חריבה — הוי להקל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 52a:4:1.english: "Is this a leniency? It is a stringency!" - And if you say: Let [this] pose a difficulty to Shmuel at the end of Keitzad Me'abrin (below, Eruvin 61b), who said: [If] one stayed on Shabbat in a ruined city, according to the Rabbis he may walk through all of it and two thousand cubits outside of it; [yet if] he placed his eiruv in a ruined city, he has only two thousand cubits from his location? And one can say: Nevertheless, ordinarily, in the normal manner, when one does not place his eiruv in a ruined city, it is [indeed] a leniency.
